examples.ko: 한옥이 산 아래에 고즈넉이 자리 잡고 있어요.
examples.en: The hanok sits quietly at the foot of the mountain.
The temple stands quietly in the forest.

examples.ko: 눈 내리는 밤, 마을이 고즈넉이 잠들어 있어요.
examples.en: On the snowy night, the village sleeps in peaceful stillness.
We sat quietly and drank tea.

examples.ko: 오래된 집이 골목 끝에 고즈넉이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: An old house remains quietly at the end of the alley.
Under the moonlight, the lake shines serenely.

explain: 풍경이나 분위기를 묘사하는 글에서 주로 보이고, 평소 대화에서는 '조용히'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '고즈넉하게'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It mostly shows up in writing that describes scenery or mood, while in ordinary conversation people more often say '조용히'. '고즈넉하게' is also used.

examples.en: The temple in the early morning is quiet and peaceful.
The snow-covered village was truly serene.
I want to read a book in a calm, quiet cafe.

examples.ko: 한옥 마을의 골목이 고즈넉해서 산책하기 좋아요.
examples.en: The alleys of the hanok village are tranquil, so they are nice for walks.
After sunset, the street became even quieter and more peaceful.
I gazed for a long time at the calmly flowing river.

explain: '조용하다'는 소리가 없다는 뜻이 중심인데, '고즈넉하다'는 호젓하고 차분한 분위기까지 느껴질 때 써요. 절, 한옥, 시골길 같은 풍경에 잘 어울려요. 도서관이 조용할 때는 '조용하다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '조용하다' is mainly about the absence of noise, while '고즈넉하다' also carries a secluded, calm mood. It suits scenes like temples, hanok, and country roads. For a quiet library, '조용하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: A deep, gentle fragrance spread through the room.
He gazed at his wife with deep feeling.
It's a night when the moonlight shines softly.
The sound of a bell echoed deeply from the mountain temple.
The rich scent of coffee reached my nose.

examples.ko: 그분은 그윽이 웃으며 제 이야기를 들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: She listened to my story with a deep, gentle smile.

explain: 깊고 은은하게 느껴지는 모습이에요. 향기, 눈빛, 달빛, 소리 같은 말과 어울려요. '깊이'는 정도만 말하지만 '그윽이'는 고요하고 은은한 느낌이 더해져요.
explain_en: It describes something that feels deep and subtle. It goes with words like fragrance, gaze, moonlight and sound. '깊이' only speaks of degree, but '그윽이' adds a quiet, subtle feeling.

examples.en: If you climb the spiral staircase, you reach the observation deck.
A snail's shell is coiled in a spiral.
The smoke rose, drawing a spiral.
Our galaxy is spiral-shaped.
The parking lot ramp spirals, so it's hard to drive.
I picked up a spiral-shaped shell on the beach.

explain: '나선형 계단'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 많이 써요. '원형'은 한 바퀴 돌아 닫힌 동그라미이고, 나선형은 돌면서 위나 바깥으로 이어지는 모양이에요. 달팽이, 소라, 은하, 계단을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is often used to modify a noun that follows, as in '나선형 계단' (spiral staircase). '원형' is a closed circle, while '나선형' keeps winding upward or outward as it turns. It often comes up when talking about snails, conch shells, galaxies and staircases.

examples.en: This writer's descriptive power is really outstanding.

examples.ko: 글쓰기 수업에서 묘사력을 기르는 연습을 많이 해요.
examples.en: In writing class we do a lot of practice to build descriptive skill.
It was a moving poem because it was written with delicate descriptive skill.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 배경 묘사력이 특히 인상적이었어요.
examples.en: That movie's depiction of the setting was especially impressive.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 묘사력이 부족해서 이야기를 짧게만 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling lacks descriptive skill, so they only tell stories briefly.

examples.ko: 묘사력 있는 문장 덕분에 풍경이 눈앞에 그려졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the vivid sentences, I could picture the scenery in front of my eyes.

explain: '표현력'은 말이나 글 전체를 두루 가리키지만, '묘사력'은 모습이나 분위기, 장면을 생생하게 그려 내는 힘에 가까워요. '뛰어나다', '부족하다', '기르다'와 자주 함께 써요. 주로 글쓰기나 소설, 영화 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: '표현력' covers expressive ability in speech and writing in general, while '묘사력' is closer to the power to paint an appearance, mood or scene vividly. It often goes with '뛰어나다', '부족하다' and '기르다'. You mostly hear it when people talk about writing, novels and films.

examples.en: The cat's eyes flashed in the darkness.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 좋은 생각이 번득여서 메모했어요.
examples.en: A good idea flashed into my mind during the meeting, so I took a note.
I can see the window glass flashing in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 그의 눈에서 번득이던 빛이 잊히지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't forget the glint that flashed in his eyes.
Lightning flashed, and soon thunder rolled.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 가끔 번득이는 아이디어를 내요.
examples.en: That student sometimes comes up with brilliant ideas.

explain: 빛이 잠깐 강하게 빛날 때 쓰고, 좋은 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때도 비유로 써요. '번뜩이다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요. 눈빛이나 아이디어를 말할 때 특히 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when light shines strongly for a moment, and figuratively when a good idea suddenly comes to mind. It is used almost the same as '번뜩이다'. It especially appears when describing a look in the eyes or an idea.

examples.ko: 동생은 선물을 받고 하루 종일 벙글벙글했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling beamed all day after getting the present.
The baby beams when it sees its mom.

examples.ko: 무슨 좋은 일이 있어요? 아침부터 벙글벙글하네요.
examples.en: Did something good happen? You've been beaming since this morning.
Dad smiled broadly at the news that I passed.

examples.ko: 벙글벙글하는 얼굴을 보니 저도 기분이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: Seeing that beaming face made me feel good too.
My friend was beaming because it was payday, and bought us a meal.

explain: 소리는 내지 않고 입을 크게 벌려 환하게 웃는 모습이에요. '벙글벙글 웃다'처럼 '웃다' 앞에 부사로 붙여서도 말해요. '싱글벙글'도 비슷하게 기분 좋은 웃음을 나타내요.
explain_en: It shows someone smiling brightly with a wide mouth but without making a sound. It is also used as an adverb before '웃다', as in '벙글벙글 웃다'. '싱글벙글' expresses a similar happy smile.

examples.en: The pyramids are truly mysterious structures.
That incident is still a mystery.
Strange, unexplainable things happened one after another.
There are many puzzling phenomena in nature.

examples.ko: 과학으로 설명할 수 없어서 더 불가사의하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: It can't be explained by science, so it feels all the more mysterious.
I read about the seven wonders of the world in a book.

explain: 이해하거나 설명할 수 없을 만큼 이상하고 놀라울 때 써요. '신기하다'는 가벼운 놀라움이고, 불가사의하다는 이유를 알 수 없는 큰 수수께끼 같은 느낌이에요. 글에서 많이 쓰고, '세계 7대 불가사의'처럼 명사 '불가사의'로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when something is so strange and amazing that it can't be understood or explained. '신기하다' is light wonder, while 불가사의하다 feels like a big riddle with no known reason. It is common in writing and also works as the noun '불가사의', as in '세계 7대 불가사의'.

examples.en: The bride is truly lovely.

examples.ko: 어여쁜 아가씨가 꽃을 들고 서 있어요.
examples.en: A pretty young lady is standing there holding flowers.

examples.ko: 아이가 웃는 모습이 참 어여뻐 보여요.
examples.en: The child looks so lovely when smiling.
My grandmother calls me her lovely granddaughter.
When spring came, the flowers bloomed beautifully.

examples.ko: 어여쁜 한복을 입은 아이들이 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: The children in pretty hanbok lined up.

explain: '예쁘다'를 좀 더 정감 있고 예스럽게 말하는 느낌이에요. 노랫말이나 시, 어른이 아이를 귀여워하는 말에서 어울려요. 친구끼리 일상 대화에서는 보통 '예쁘다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels like a warmer, slightly old-fashioned way of saying '예쁘다'. It suits song lyrics, poems, and adults fondly talking about children. In everyday talk between friends, people usually just say '예쁘다'.

examples.ko: 새 직장에서 저만 천덕꾸러기가 된 기분이에요.
examples.en: At my new job I feel like I'm the only one treated as a nuisance.

examples.ko: 동생이 태어난 뒤로 저는 집에서 천덕꾸러기 취급을 받았어요.
examples.en: After my sibling was born, I was treated like a nuisance at home.

examples.ko: 천덕꾸러기로 남은 낡은 소파를 결국 버렸어요.
examples.en: I finally threw out the old sofa that nobody wanted.

examples.ko: 저는 어디에 가도 천덕꾸러기는 아니었으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope I'm never the unwanted one wherever I go.
The game console that was once popular is now a nuisance.

examples.ko: 모두가 천덕꾸러기라고 놀렸지만 그 아이는 꿋꿋했어요.
examples.en: Everyone teased him as a burden, but the child stayed strong.

explain: 사람뿐 아니라 쓸모없어져서 푸대접받는 물건에도 써요. '천덕꾸러기 취급을 받다', '천덕꾸러기가 되다'가 자주 쓰는 형태예요. '골칫덩어리'는 문제를 일으켜 곤란한 존재이고, 천덕꾸러기는 사람들에게 푸대접받는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: It is used for people and also for things that became useless and are treated poorly. Common forms are '천덕꾸러기 취급을 받다' and '천덕꾸러기가 되다'. '골칫덩어리' is someone who causes trouble, while a 천덕꾸러기 is the one who gets treated badly.

en: turbulent; full of ups and downs

examples.en: My grandmother told me about her life full of ups and downs.
That singer's life has really been full of ups and downs.

examples.ko: 파란만장했던 한 해를 보내고 새해를 맞았어요.
examples.en: We saw off a turbulent year and welcomed the new one.

examples.ko: 파란만장하게 살아온 그분의 이야기가 책으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The story of that person, who lived through many ups and downs, came out as a book.

examples.ko: 그의 인생은 파란만장하지만 늘 웃음을 잃지 않아요.
examples.en: His life is full of turmoil, but he never loses his smile.

examples.ko: 파란만장하다는 말은 그분의 삶에 딱 맞아요.
examples.en: The word 'eventful' fits that person's life perfectly.

explain: 행복과 불행이 크게 오르내린 긴 삶이나 이야기에 써요. 주로 '삶, 인생, 일생' 같은 말을 꾸미고, 하루짜리 일에는 어색해요. 일이 많았던 한 해에는 '다사다난하다'도 써요.
explain_en: It is used for a long life or story with big swings between joy and hardship. It usually modifies words like '삶', '인생' and '일생' and sounds odd for a single day's events. For a busy, eventful year, '다사다난하다' is also used.
